intro: Djibouti is a small country at the mouth of the Red Sea whose port and military bases make it strategically important.

chapters.title: Afar and Issa
text: Afar and Somali Issa peoples have lived here for centuries as herders and traders, along routes linking Africa and Arabia.

chapters.title: French Somaliland
text: France took control in the 1880s, and a railway was built from Djibouti to Addis Ababa. It was called French Somaliland, then the French Territory of the Afars and Issas.

chapters.title: Independence
text: Djibouti became independent in 1977. Ismaïl Omar Guelleh has been president since 1999.

highlight.title: Location
highlight.text: About 10% of world trade passes Djibouti through the Bab-el-Mandeb strait.
